results.name: Tacos al Pastor at El Huequito
results.why_it_is_special: Opened in 1959, El Huequito is widely regarded as the first taquería to serve tacos al pastor in Mexico City. Its marinade features achiote and guajillo chile — a recipe unchanged for decades.

results.name: Tacos al Pastor at El Tizoncito
results.why_it_is_special: El Tizoncito is credited with adding the now-beloved pineapple to tacos al pastor in the mid-1960s. It remains a local institution with ~13 locations across the city.

results.name: Suadero Tacos at Tacos El Paisa
results.why_it_is_special: Suadero is the only taco style to originate in Mexico City — made from a cut of beef simmered in oil for hours. Tacos El Paisa draws nightly crowds of locals for this quintessentially chilango taco.

results.name: Tacos de Tripa & Suadero at Los Cocuyos
results.why_it_is_special: A tiny, perpetually busy stand famous for its tripe tacos — soft yet crispy, never chewy — considered an obligatory visit for any taco enthusiast. Open late into the night.

results.name: Tacos at El Vilsito
results.why_it_is_special: By day a car-repair shop, by night an excellent taquería. This beloved local oddity serves outstanding tacos and captures the spirit of Mexico City's street-food culture.

results.name: Barbacoa de Borrego at Barbacoa Henry
results.why_it_is_special: Barbacoa in Mexico City means slow-cooked lamb served weekend mornings, often accompanied by consomé and Norteño music. Barbacoa Henry is considered one of the best in the city for this ritual dish.

results.name: Churros at Churrería El Moro
results.why_it_is_special: A Mexico City institution for churros and hot chocolate, El Moro has been serving generations of chilangos. It's the city's most famous churrería.

results.name: Tlacoyos & Antojitos at Mercado de la Merced
results.why_it_is_special: One of the largest and oldest markets in Mexico City, La Merced is where locals shop for produce and eat traditional street food — tamales, tlacoyos (oval corn-dough patties stuffed with beans and topped with cheese, cactus, and salsa), tortas, and more.

results.name: Tostadas & Mole Enchiladas at Mercado de Coyoacán
results.why_it_is_special: Located in the charming, historic neighbourhood of Coyoacán, this market is a favourite for traditional tostadas, tamales, and enchiladas doused in rich mole — all in a setting far from the tourist mainstream.

results.name: Quesabirria at Tacos Don Juan
results.why_it_is_special: Quesabirria — birria-dipped, cheese-filled tacos — has become a local obsession. Tacos Don Juan in Condesa is singled out for making an incredible version of this dish.

results.name: Pozole at Pozolería Teoixtla
results.why_it_is_special: When locals want a break from tacos, pozole (hominy-and-meat soup with a pre-Hispanic lineage) is the go-to comfort food. Pozolería Teoixtla in Roma is a neighbourhood favourite for this celebratory dish.

results.name: Exotic Ingredients at Mercado de San Juan
results.why_it_is_special: Mexico City's most famous market for exotic and gourmet ingredients — from edible insects to imported cheeses. A destination for adventurous eaters and professional chefs alike.
